pyqs.answer: Magnitude 1126 kJ/mol of reaction as written; ΔrH°=−1125.8 kJ/mol
pyqs.independentSolution: Products=2(−286)+2(−297)=−1166;reactants=2(−20.1)+3(0)=−40.2;difference=−1125.8. Magnitude rounds1126. Halving equation would halve reaction enthalpy.

pyqs.independentSolution: HCl(aq) formation per mole=−164/2−83=−165. Then ΔfH(Al₂Cl₆ aq)=−1200+6(−165)=−2190; subtract dissolution−663: solid=−1527. Direct Hess sum−1200+3(−164)+6(−83)+663=−1527.
pyqs.adaptation: Writes heat released as negative ΔH; retains original formal Al₂Cl₆ notation and all states without asserting the aqueous molecular species.

targetQuestionText: For 2H₂S(g) + 3O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) + 2SO₂(g), the standard formation enthalpies of H₂S(g), H₂O(l) and SO₂(g) are −20.1, −286.0 and −297.0 kJ/mol. Find the magnitude of the reaction enthalpy, to the nearest integer, for the equation as written.
